profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary: Software engineer with 7+ years of experience in all areas of the software development cycle.  Skilled in the research, design, and development of high-traffic, high-availability systems.  Proven ability to lead development teams to achieve ambitious targets.  Recognized and awarded for the ability to go above and beyond, identifying areas of improvement and taking initiative to propose and implement solutions.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer II
positions.description:
The Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) organization powers Amazon's global network of fulfillment centres (FC).  The FC's move millions of units of inventory daily, employ tens of thousands of people, and are built and evolved by cross-team software and hardware innovations.  At Amazon, my problem space was the Outbound Sortation process of customer fulfillment.  I built and owned numerous mission-critical, Tier-1 software services that run Amazon's highest throughput FC's.

I researched, designed, developed, and delivered an optimization to the Rebinning process for Amazon Fulfillment Engine (AFE) centres.  AFE centres are the highest throughput sites and Rebinning is a sub-process in Outbound Sortation where items for the same shipment are recombined.  This optimization yielded an 8% reduction in the overall time to Rebin shipments and was successfully deployed to all AFE sites, spanning North America and Japan.

Additionally, I designed, implemented, and tested various components of a new Tier-1 software service to power all AFE sites internationally.  This new system was a complete redesign and leveraged various AWS technologies including DynamoDB, RDS, SQS, and SNS.  I played a critical role to see this new system through from inception to an international launch and migration.

I also played a critical role in the design, development, and launch of a Tier-1 greenfield project to build a lower-level warehouse control system that would replace systems typically external to the Amazon software infrastructure.  We successfully launched the first-ever warehouse without external vendor software in Amazon history while on-site in Europe.

During my most recent annual review at Amazon, I received the second highest technical rating of "Exceeds" and the highest leadership principle rating of "Role Model".  I have also represented my team for peak support in Japan and was on-site to launch the first-ever AFE in Europe during a month-long assignment.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
SiteScout (acquired by Centro) is a leading Ad Tech company in the Real-time Bidding (RTB) advertising auction space with a focus on being self-service.  SiteScout currently processes an upwards of 31 billion bid requests daily and is integrated with 73 Ad Exchanges.  SiteScout was acquired by Centro during my time there, aligning it with their goal to unify all the disparate pieces of digital media operations into a single platform.

At SiteScout I researched, designed, implemented, and released a coordinate targeting feature for mobile ads.  This feature leveraged GPS information from mobile bid requests to allow advertisers to target arbitrarily granular areas of interest.  For example, this feature enabled customers to pinpoint areas to aggressively run their ads and also to define black-out areas for their campaigns.

With great volume and server count came a great difficultly troubleshooting live issues.  I took the initiative to eliminate an unsolved technical issue of having poor visibility into live application logs when it mattered.  I researched and built a real-time log viewing and archiving system which enabled the monitoring and filtering of aggregated logs from arbitrary server clusters.  This system was built using Kibana, Syslog, LogStash, and ElasticSearch technologies.

Additionally, I innovated a flexible tool to simulate bid requests from various Ad Exchanges.  This tool enabled the realization of a previously unachieved technical goal to replay an arbitrary amount of journaled bid requests for the purpose of analyzing bidder behaviour, algorithmic tuning, strategy comparison, and other experimentation.

I also led the adoption of StatsD, Metrics (Coda Hale), and Graphite, establishing visibility into ad hoc metrics and analytics at the company.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Acuity Ads is an Ad Tech company that participates in the Real-time Bidding (RTB) advertising auction space.  The RTB space is a high-traffic, high-performance environment as Acuity Ads receives an upwards of 8 billion bid requests daily and is expected to respond to each request within 50 ms.  As a Demand-side Platform (DSP) company, Acuity Ads automates the purchase of online advertising on behalf of advertisers, provides consumer targeting capabilities, and allows advertisers to monitor campaign performance.

At Acuity Ads I led the initiative to introduce the usage of Hadoop to the company for the purpose of analyzing user profile and bid request information.  I successfully launched a single-node cluster prototype, processing over one billion user profile records to generate various reports where there was no previously existing visibility.

I delivered a complete redesign of the user profile binary record structure, encapsulating demographic data from 3rd party sources, defining new dynamic records to store campaign interaction history and segment information, and implemented new formulas that govern the accumulation and decay of data.

I also innovated previously nonexistent tools to simulate bid requests from all integrated ad exchanges and to interface with a real-time NoSQL datastore to lookup, create, and modify user profile records.  Working across the full system, I also participated in the development of bidder targeting filters, revenue and stats components, and the integration of video (VAST) ad companion banners.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
LyricFind is the leading provider of licensed song lyric and music data services. They have acquired licensing from over 2,000 publishers and are expanding to include indie labels and other territories.  LyricFind powers sites and mobile applications including: Microsoft Bing, Lyrics.com, Shazam, Rhapsody, and Virgin Media.

I led the research, proposal, design, development, and launch of several critical projects at LyricFind.

The first was a complete redesign of the existing core company web service.  I investigated performance, scalability, and maintainability issues with the existing system and code base, establishing the redesign project.  I then delivered a new RESTful web service, leveraging MVC design, system-wide caching using Apache JCS, and integration with a new Solr search subsystem.  The result was a greatly simplified and more powerful API supporting multiple music ID systems, greater search capability, new output formats, and client customizations.

The second was the proposal, design, development, and delivery of a tracking subsystem with which to capture API usage information, statistics, and system performance metrics.  This system provided the company with a revolutionary analysis-driven approach to identify deficient areas of content and licensing, better understand user behaviour, monitor system and cache performance, and to innovate new services.  This new system also eliminated the need to perform frequent and problematic database replication.

positions.title: Team Lead / Software Engineer
positions.description:
Become Japan is a Japanese shopping search engine company that aggregates over 15 million products from over 30,000 merchants.  These products are matched with buying guides, reviews, and related articles by an integrated web search system, providing users with a new and informed way to shop.  Become Japan's product results were integrated by leading Japanese search engines, stressing the need for scalable, highly available systems.

I led a team of developers to launch a variety of projects in an ambitious, fast-paced environment.  We often juggled multiple projects including: site renewals, new site creation, stabilization of systems, prototyping of new concept sites, SEO improvements, and tracking improvements for automated SEM.

I played a critical role in the company, often collaborating with multiple teams (web designers, media producers, product managers, account managers, system admins, and developers) to push projects to completion.  This often required overcoming very challenging language and cultural obstacles.

I received a quarterly MVP award for self-initiated research and improvements in the area of SEO, achieving a daily organic revenue increase of 400%.

positions.title: Assistant Language Teacher
positions.description:
The Japan Exchange and Teaching (JET) Programme is a government-affiliated program which promotes grass-roots international exchange between Japan and other nations.  Each year, 5,000 participants are selected from 36 countries and placed all over Japan, from megacities to remote island towns.

I was placed in Saitama City, Saitama Prefecture, where I taught in the public school system.  Working with more than 36 different Japanese English teachers, while rotating between 6 schools, proved to be the ultimate test in adaptation.  My greatest challenge was to overcome language and cultural differences to build strong relationships with other teachers.  These positive relationships were a strong foundation for effective teamwork and the fostering of successful classrooms.
